title: Designing a library system
idea: A small LLD turns requirements into classes: find the nouns, give each one clear data and duties, then trace one use case through them.
points: Requirements: search books, borrow and return copies, cap loans, charge late fines.
`Book` is the title; `BookCopy` is one physical item that can be lent.
`LoanService` holds the rules; `Catalog` only finds available copies.
Fines vary by library, so `FinePolicy` is an injected strategy.

hero.title: Borrow and return, step by step

messages.label: available('Dune')
messages.note: The desk searches by title. The catalog returns only copies not on loan.

messages.label: [c1, c2]
messages.note: Copies, not books, come back: each copy is lent on its own.

messages.label: borrow(ana, c1, day)
messages.note: `LoanService` checks the copy is free and the member is under the limit.

messages.label: onLoan = true
messages.note: The copy is marked, and a `Loan` records member, copy and due day.

messages.label: Loan
messages.note: The caller keeps the `Loan` to return it later.

messages.label: giveBack(loan, day)
messages.note: Returning frees the copy and removes the loan from the member.

messages.label: feeFor(daysLate)
messages.note: The fine rule is delegated, so a new policy needs no edit to `LoanService`.

code.title: The whole model
code.caption: Four entities, a catalog, a fine policy and one service. Add a `CappedFine` policy that never charges more than 50, and inject it.

walk.text: Entities hold data: a `Book` title, its lendable `BookCopy`, a `Member`, and the `Loan` linking them.
`Catalog` answers one question: which copies of this title are free?
`FlatFine` is one `FinePolicy`: any object with `feeFor(daysLate)`. The service receives it.
Validate first with guard clauses: the copy must be free, the member under the limit.
Then change state: record a `Loan` due in 14 days, mark the copy, add it to the member.
Returning refuses a loan already returned, then frees the copy and asks the policy for the fee.
Wire everything at the edge: a small composition root.

pitfalls: Do not merge `Book` and `BookCopy`; one title can have many lendable copies.
Keep rules out of entities like `Member`; put them in a service or policy.
State requirements and assumptions aloud before drawing classes in an interview.

quiz.why: The first call finds the copy free and marks it. The second sees `onLoan` is true and returns early.

takeaway: Nouns become classes, rules live in services, varying rules become strategies.

starters: How would I add reservations when every copy is on loan?
Should Loan be a class or just a record in a repository?
How do I draw this as a UML class diagram?
